1. Yes, and the chart shows it. Guidance comes through the 9th house and Guru, the guru and dharma. Following it depends on the lagna and the 5th, the self and its judgment. An afflicted 9th, or a functionally malefic Guru controlling it, brings wrong guides and false gurus. A bad Guru aspecting the lagna gives a native who listens to no one, and a bad Budha gives one who talks more than he hears. Timing matters too: good guidance tends to arrive, and be taken, in the daśās of the grahas that rule the 9th or control it by aspect. Some people only come to the astrologer when it is already too late to act, and that too is written in their karma.

2. The chart is the field of one’s prārabdha, the karma already ripening, and it shows what can grow and roughly how much. Kriyamāṇa, the karma one does now, works against it, and most people realise far less of their promise than their chart allows. Ordinary effort only lifts the results within that promise. Kriyamāṇa can subdue prārabdha itself on one condition: it must be done as prāyaścitta karma, the action that answers the specific debt the chart shows, and with a saṅkalpa free of any vikalpa. A resolve that keeps an alternative open, or wavers between paths, divides the effort and leaves the prārabdha in charge. Taken up with an undivided saṅkalpa, the right prāyaścitta can carry a native’s wealth and career beyond what the chart alone would give. The capacity for that resolve is itself in the chart, in the lagna and the 3rd.

Rāhu in Makara, Ketu in Karka: The Earth Lagnas
4 December 2026 to 22 June 2028

Rāhu's transit through Makara acts on all three earth lagnas at once. His 5th and 9th aspects fall on Vṛṣabha and Kanyā, and Ketu, transiting Karka, casts his 7th aspect on Makara. The whole earth triplicity comes under the nodal axis.

Vṛṣabha Lagna

Rāhu, lord of the 5th, transits the 9th. He ties intelligence, children, education and speculation to fortune, higher knowledge, teachers and long journeys. Foreign teachers, unconventional philosophy and advanced study come forward, and his aspects on the lagna and the 5th reinforce them.

Ketu, lord of the 11th, occupies the 3rd. Siblings grow distant, casual associations thin, and friendships become selective. His aspects on the 7th, 9th and 11th carry this detachment into partnership, belief and the social circle.

Until July 2027, Guru, lord of the 8th and 11th, aspects Rāhu. Fortune arrives through a teacher, the father or a benefactor, but the 8th attaches obligations and sudden turns through inheritance, insurance or research funding.

From 8 to 20 April 2027, Ketu controls Śani, the yogakāraka. An important professional offer arrives with a binding commitment. It is substantial, and its terms must be read twice before signing.

Ketu, as 11th lord aspecting the 7th, is a prime māraka. Guard the spouse's health and your own vitality from 9 February to 13 May 2027 and around the eclipse of 2 August 2027.

Fortune is most generous from August 2027 to June 2028, when Śani's aspect on Rāhu joins fortune to career. In January 2028 an exalted Maṅgala joins Rāhu, bringing travel abroad with the spouse.

Kanyā Lagna

Rāhu, co-lord of the lagna, transits the 5th and aspects the lagna. Intellectual ambition, education, creative work, romance and speculation rise, and with them the drive to build an independent identity.

Ketu, lord of the 7th, occupies the 11th. Partnerships bring gains, and dependence on those gains falls away. Some friendships end of their own accord. His aspects on the 3rd, 5th and 7th put communication, creative commitments and intimate relationships under review.

This transit can produce the finest creative or intellectual work of a lifetime. Rāhu in the 5th gives an unusually persistent appetite for knowledge and output. The danger is mental excess: failing to tell a worthwhile inspiration from an obsession that eats time and returns little.

Higher education, research and creative work peak between June and December 2027, often through institutions or opportunities far from home. Large-scale technology, digital platforms, infrastructure and applied research are the fields.

Partnerships bring financial or professional gains without chasing, but speculation still needs research. Maṅgala is a prime māraka from 9 March to 26 April 2027, and Śani in the 8th is one from 23 June to 10 September 2027. Guard health, savings and financial exposure in both windows.

The transit favours children and their growth, and elder siblings turn toward dharma, observance and philosophy.

Makara Lagna

Makara takes the most direct impact. Rāhu, lord of the 9th, occupies the lagna, and Ketu, lord of the 3rd, aspects it from the 7th. Both nodes act on the self and tie changes in identity, body and ambition to marriage, partnership and existing commitments.

Rāhu's aspects on the 5th and 9th strengthen education, intelligence, fortune and higher pursuits. A foreign connection or an unconventional line of work becomes central. Above all, the native acquires the specialised qualification that sets the course of the career.

From 23 July 2027, Śani, the lagna lord, aspects Rāhu. Ambition gains discipline, and the drive to advance becomes deliberate, sustained and lasting.

Ketu in the 7th brings a reassessment of marriage and business partnerships. An old commitment is renegotiated, and a close friend takes an important place in the relationship as confidant, go-between or rival.

February to May 2027 is the hardest span. A weak Maṅgala beside Ketu in the 7th brings disputes over home, money and marital expectations.

Rāhu on the lagna brings vāta disturbances: dryness, irregular sleep and nervous agitation. Warm meals at regular hours and a steady routine settle them. In January 2028 Sūrya joins Rāhu, and the body runs hot and tired.

The wider social circle contracts as the native chooses associations with care. Fortune slows in August 2027, while the longer transit consolidates the professional direction.

NOTE on Interpretation:

These are whole-house indications for the three lagnas in general. Refine them for each native with the Chalit bhāva cusps, the nodes' aspects by degree with a 20° orb, the tārās they move through, and above all the running daśā.

The transit sets the field of possible events. The natal chart decides how they take shape, and the daśā decides which of them come to fruit.

posts.author: VEDANJANAM
posts.text:
Yes. Work through it in this order, and the net result usually becomes clear.

1. Start with the natal promise and the daśā. A transit can only deliver what the birth chart holds and the running daśā allows. Of the grahas aspecting the house, the ones whose daśā or antardaśā is running carry the result. The others colour it.
2. Look for Śani and Guru together. When both aspect a house, or its lord, the matter becomes possible. Read them through their lordships: they decide what the event is.
3. Trace aspect chains back to the head. If one aspecting graha is itself aspected by another, the second controls it. A one-way aspect is very strong, and the chain head decides the direction of the result.
4. Weigh each aspect by exactness and position. Aspects work by degree with an orb, and the closest to exact dominates at that moment. An aspect on the bhāva madhya in the Chalit gives full results; one near the ārambha or the anta gives about a quarter.
5. Judge each graha's nature and strength. Functional nature decides which polarity a graha gives, and strength decides how far it goes.
6. Refine with the tārā. Even a good graha moving through vadha or another bad tārā gives suboptimal results.
7. Sambandha only modifies. Conjunctions among the transiting grahas change the flavour of the result, never its direction.

Mixed aspects don't cancel out. Both results come: the benefic brings the event, and the malefic brings its cost. Their timing separates by exactness, so each graha dominates while its aspect is closest. The slow grahas (Śani, Guru and the nodes) set the background for the year. Maṅgala, Sūrya and Candra trigger the event within it, on the day their aspects become exact.

posts.text: 1. Praśna and natal charts: The natal chart holds the prārabdha, fixed at birth. The praśna chart is the sky at the moment a question is asked sincerely, and it shows that prārabdha as it stands now, after everything the native has done since. That later action is kriyamāṇa, and it is why the two charts can differ. Ordinary kriyamāṇa only moves results within the natal promise, and then the praśna agrees with the natal chart. Kriyamāṇa done as prāyaścitta karma, with a saṅkalpa free of any vikalpa, can subdue the prārabdha itself. The praśna then shows an outcome the natal chart alone would not give. The praśna also guides what comes next, because it shows what action the moment calls for. A difference can also have other causes: the natal promise may be real but not yet due, the question may have been asked casually or as a test, which voids the praśna, or the birth time may be wrong.

posts.author: VEDANJANAM
posts.text:
2. Astrology and subconscious patterns: Yes. Jyotiṣa calls them saṃskāras and vāsanās: impressions left by past karma that drive present behaviour before the native knows it. Candra is the mind, the 4th the inner feeling, the 5th the stored merit and tendencies of past lives, the 8th what is hidden, and the 12th sleep and what lies below awareness. Aspect chains show how one pattern triggers the next, and retrograde grahas show patterns that keep repeating. The results come from what the native does under these patterns. That is kriyamāṇa shaped by vāsanā. Seeing the pattern is the first step to breaking it.

3. "May and may not": It comes from weak method or fear of being wrong. A reading done properly, the natal promise, then the daśā, then the transit, weighed in order, gives a decision. Real uncertainty exists only where karma is adṛḍha, open to change by present action. Even then it should be stated as a condition, not a hedge: "this will happen unless you do this." "It may or may not happen" tells the client nothing
posts.my_take: Saṃskāras and vāsanās drive behaviour before we even know it. Candra, the 4th, 5th, 8th, 12th, plus retro grahas for patterns that keep repeating. Seeing the pattern is the first step to breaking it.

posts.text:
Sign to sign is the accurate method. Both charts sit in the same sky, so a partner's Śani at 12° Tulā is at 12° Tulā for you too. Lining up the two ascendants moves the partner's grahas to places they never occupied, so the "house to house" overlay has no basis.

How to read it:

1. Place the partner's grahas by degree in your chart. Count the houses from your own lagna, using the Chalit cusps. The partner's Guru in your 7th bhāva, near the madhya, works fully on your marriage. Near the edge, it gives about a quarter.
2. Read the aspects by degree and orb. Look at what the partner's grahas aspect in your chart: your lagna, lagna lord, 7th, 7th lord, Śukra and Candra. Aspects come first here, as they do everywhere.
3. Judge each graha by your lagna's lordships. The partner's Śani works in your chart as Śani works for your lagna. For a Tulā native, he is the yogakāraka. For a Karka native, he is the 7th and 8th lord.
4. Do it both ways. Read the partner's grahas in your chart and yours in the partner's. Compatibility is the overlap where both directions support each other.
5. Keep the natal promise and the daśā first. No overlay creates a marriage that one chart denies, and the daśās decide when the bond tightens or strains.

Nakṣatra matching (kūṭa milan) is a separate test and runs alongside this.

A praśna is needed in a few cases:

1. The birth data is missing or doubtful. The praśna then stands in for the natal chart.
2. The question is specific and immediate. A lost object, a particular deal, an illness in crisis, whether a journey will succeed. The natal chart shows the broad promise; the praśna answers the question in front of you.
3. Kriyamāṇa may have moved the result. If the native has done serious prāyaścitta, the praśna shows where the prārabdha stands now, which the natal chart alone cannot.
4. You need confirmation or a choice of action. When the natal reading is close, the praśna confirms the timing and shows what the moment calls for.

A praśna must come from a sincere question. Cast casually, or as a test, it is void.

posts.text:
Daśā results are read from the D1. The D9 as a separate chart is not needed, and conjunctions or house placements inside a D9 mean nothing. The navāṃśa itself still matters, as a division position.

The daśā lord's navāṃśa position grades its daśā. Varāhamihira does exactly this in Bṛhajjātaka 8.5–7: a graha at its exact exaltation degree gives a full daśā (sampūrṇā), and one at its exact debilitation degree gives an empty one (riktā). A graha descending from exaltation is raised by a friendly or exalted navāṃśa, and one rising from debilitation is lowered by an enemy or debilitated navāṃśa. A well-placed graha in a debilitated or enemy navāṃśa gives mixed results (miśraphalā). 

So, the navāṃśa grades the daśā. It never cancels the D1 dignity.

Read the daśā lord's sign, house, aspects and lordship from the D1, and its strength in the Chalit bhāva. Then refine with its navāṃśa position, read through the lord of that navāṃśa.

posts.text:
Rāśi and Chalit: What a Graha Is and Where It Acts

The distinction between the Rāśi Cakra and Bhāva Chalit is based upon two questions: what is the condition of a graha, and where does it produce its results?

Rāśi Cakra establishes the graha's condition. Its rāśi determines exaltation, debilitation, friendship and enmity, while its lordships establish its functional nature. These remain unchanged in the Chalit.

Chalit establishes its field of operation. Bhāvas are calculated from the lagna and meridian and do not necessarily coincide with rāśi boundaries.

In the Śrīpati system, Madhya is the bhāva centre, where its influence is strongest. The 1st madhya is the lagna degree, the 10th is the meridian, and the intervening madhyas are obtained by trisecting the quadrants. Sandhi is the boundary between successive bhāvas, halfway between their madhyas. Ārambha and Anta are the opening and closing sandhis, between which each bhāva extends through its madhya.

Since the quadrants are generally unequal, bhāvas also differ in extent.

Consider a lagna at 25° Mithuna, with the 1st bhāva extending from 10° Mithuna to 10° Karka. A graha at 5° Karka occupies the second rāśi from the lagna but falls within the 1st bhāva. It retains its dignity and dispositor in Karka while producing results concerning the body, constitution and self. Its rāśi has not changed. Only its bhāva classification differs.

How Strongly Does It Deliver?

Śrīpati employs the rule of three, or trairāśika, to calculate the proportion of bhāva results. At the madhya, the result is full; at either sandhi, much reduced. Between them, the contribution varies proportionately with distance.

posts.author: VEDANJANAM
posts.text:
There are authoritative root texts, but no single one stands over the whole of Jyotiṣa the way Vālmīki stands over the Rāmāyaṇa.

The most secure is Varāhamihira's Bṛhajjātaka (6th century). It is firmly dated, its text is stable across manuscripts, and Bhaṭṭotpala's commentary fixes its reading. Varāha himself cites older teachers (Maya, Yavana, Parāśara, Satyācārya, Jīvaśarman), so even he is summarising an older tradition.

The Bṛhat Parāśara Horāśāstra carries the name of the root ṛṣi, but its text is the least settled: editions differ in chapters, verse order and content.

The Laghu Pārāśarī distils the Pārāśarī doctrine of functional nature and daśā into a short, stable text, and that is why it serves as the working authority for that method and is the most clear distillation of the true Indian method of astrology.

Jaimini's Upadeśa Sūtras are the root for the Jaimini method, and the Sārāvalī and Horā Sāra stand close behind Varāha.

So Jyotiṣa has several roots, one for each method, rather than one root for everything. The practical answer is the one I gave earlier: choose one text, learn its method end to end, and don't mix it with another.

posts.author: VEDANJANAM
posts.text:
Only Budha and Śukra can be retrograde and combust at once. They turn retrograde at inferior conjunction, when they are nearest to the Earth and closest to Sūrya. Maṅgala, Guru and Śani are retrograde only when they stand opposite Sūrya, so they can never be combust while retrograde. The classical orbs shrink for a retrograde graha: Budha 12° instead of 14°, Śukra 8° instead of 10°.

Apply the two rules in order. First retrogression, then combustion. Under a functionally benefic Sūrya, Sūrya lends strength and takes over the graha's role. Under a functionally malefic Sūrya, the combustion is very bad. If Śukra rules the 6th or 11th, he behaves badly when combust even under a benefic Sūrya, and in bad dignity he becomes terrible.

Together, the graha's matters keep returning, and each time they are handled through Sūrya: the father, authority, the state or the native's own ego. Whether that turns out well depends on Sūrya's functional nature.

posts.author: VEDANJANAM
posts.text:
Rectification works because the D1 and the daśā respond to time differently. The lagna moves about 1° every 4 minutes and carries the bhāva cusps with it. Candra moves about 0.5° an hour, which shifts every daśā start by weeks for a few minutes of error and by months for an hour. Matching those shifts to the events of a life narrows the time.

Begin with 8–10 dated events: marriage, children, job changes, moves, a parent's death, surgeries, accidents. Hard events serve better than happy ones. Fix the lagna sign from the aspects on the lagna and its lord, the grahas in it and the sign itself, against the person's build and temperament. Then move the time until the antardaśā and pratyantardaśā changes line up with the events, each falling in the period of a graha that controls the relevant bhāva. As the time moves, grahas cross sandhis, and the right time puts each event's significator near the madhya of the matching bhāva. Confirm each event by Śani and Guru aspecting the relevant house or its lord, with the trigger crossing the Chalit madhya. The ṣaṣṭyaṃśa of the lagna, about 2 minutes of birth time each, settles what remains.

posts.author: VEDANJANAM
posts.text: The rāśi gives each graha its nature, through its dignity and lordships. The Chalit gives the bhāva where it delivers, fully at the madhya and a quarter near a sandhi. Grahas in one sign may sit in different bhāvas, and they are conjunct only within the mean of their orbs. Each graha carries its partners' houses, and the strongest by ṣaḍbala leads. Combustion follows Sūrya's functional nature. Within 1°, graha-yuddha is decided by śara. Sinking needs a partner combust under a malefic Sūrya, or below 90% of its required ṣaḍbala in a duḥsthāna. Kendra and trikoṇa lords form rāja yoga, and a node with a trikoṇa lord in a kendra is a yogakāraka unless the 8th or 11th lord joins. Aspects give the primary result.

posts.text:
The teacher comes when the student is ready and the time is right, in the daśās of the grahas that rule or aspect the 9th. Until then, prepare. Learn one root text end to end without mixing others; it never contradicts itself.

Test every rule on charts whose lives you know, and keep a notebook of what held and what failed. Ask precise questions, with the chart, the rule and where it failed, and good teachers will make time for you.

Work through charts with one or two serious fellow students, because explaining a chart exposes what you haven't understood. Be an adhikārī, a student who does the work, and the right teacher tends to find you.

posts.author: VEDANJANAM
posts.text:
There is no fixed number, because the names you list are of different kinds. Some are classical divisions of Jyotiṣa, some are methods within one division, and some are single texts or modern systems.

The classical divisions. Jyotiṣa has three skandhas: Siddhānta (astronomy and calculation), Saṃhitā (mundane matters and omens) and Horā (individual charts). Later tradition counts six aṅgas: jātaka (nativities), gola (spherical astronomy), gaṇita (calculation), praśna (horary), muhūrta (electional) and nimitta (omens).

Classical methods within Horā

1. Pārāśarī: Bṛhat Parāśara Horāśāstra. Laghu Pārāśarī is a single text distilling its doctrine of functional nature and daśā.
2. Varāhī: Varāhamihira's Bṛhajjātaka, with Sārāvalī and Horā Sāra close behind it.
3. Jaimini: Upadeśa Sūtras
3. Tājika: annual charts (varṣaphala).
4. Praśna: horary.
5. Nāḍī: palm-leaf traditions such as the Bhṛgu, Śukra and Dhruva Nāḍīs.
6. Svarodaya and the cakras: Narapati's Narapatijayacaryā and the Sarvatobhadra Cakra.

Modern systems (20th century)

1. Lal Kitāb: a set of Urdu books (1939–1952), attributed to Pandit Roop Chand Joshi, known for its remedies, often strange.
2. Krishnamurti Paddhati (KP): K. S. Krishnamurti's sub-lord system.
3. Bhṛgu Nandi Nāḍī (BNN): a modern method built on Nāḍī principles, popularised by R. G. Rao.

The classical methods have root texts. The modern systems stand on their founders' credibility.

posts.author: VEDANJANAM
posts.text:
A bhāva keeps its domain in every condition. Affliction makes the domain suffered; strength makes it commanded. 

A bad 6th gives disease, debt and enemies; a good 6th gives mastery over disease, lending, the judge and the lawyer.

The 8th is mind, chronic disease, health and death; a strong 8th removes fear of death and pushes toward helping professions in those domains, strongest in the 8th's daśā.
posts.my_take: Good reminder for chart reading. A bad 6th doesn't take the domain away, it makes you suffer it; a strong 6th makes you command it. Same house, two very different lives .. thats why strength matters more than labels.

posts.author: VEDANJANAM
posts.text:
Anuradha ji, in making this comparison, you have hit the nail on the head. I have thought about this for a long time, and here is the distillation. 

Kālapuruṣa is Time embodied as a cosmic person.

His body is the twelve rāśis, Meṣa at the head, Mīna at the feet (Bṛhajjātaka 1.4).

His faculties are the grahas: Sūrya the ātman, Candra the mind, Maṅgala strength, Budha speech, Guru knowledge and happiness, Śukra desire, Śani sorrow (Bṛhajjātaka 2.1).

His elements are the grahas too: Maṅgala fire, Budha earth, Guru space, Śukra water, Śani air.

The doṣas and dhātus follow them, from Sūrya's bone and Candra's blood to Śukra's reproductive essence.

At birth the cosmic body becomes personal. The lagna is where the macrocosm meets the native.

The bhāvas lay the Kālapuruṣa's limbs across the native's body and life.

A graha's rāśi and bhāva show how its faculty, element and tissue appear in the native.

The cosmos is the body of Īśvara, as the native's body is the body of the jīva.

Kālapuruṣa is that cosmic body seen as time.

Yathā brahmāṇḍe tathā piṇḍe is one relation of body to indweller, holding at both scales.

The Devī is mind, space, air, fire, water and earth (Saundaryalaharī 35).

Earth sits at the mūlādhāra, water at the svādhiṣṭhāna, fire at the maṇipūra, air in the heart, space above it, mind between the brows (Saundaryalaharī 9).

Along the spine the grahas stand in order: Budha, Śukra, Maṅgala, Śani, Guru; Candra at the ājñā; Sūrya at the crown.

She dwells in the mūlādhāra, pierces the three granthis and mounts the thousand-petalled lotus (Lalitā Sahasranāma).

The Kālapuruṣa in the sky and the kuṇḍalinī in the body are one order, read outward and inward.

The self has four quarters: waking, dreaming, deep sleep and turīya (Māṇḍūkya 3–7).

Waking is the sthūla śarīra, dreaming the sūkṣma, deep sleep the kāraṇa.

Viśvarūpā jāgariṇī svapantī taijasātmikā, suptā prājñātmikā turyā sarvāvasthā-vivarjitā (Lalitā Sahasranāma).

Physical laws hold in open systems but cannot predict them.

The living being exchanges matter, energy and information, runs far from equilibrium, and emerges from its organisation.

Physics constrains the living; it does not determine them. Physics measures only the sthūla.

The sūkṣma and the kāraṇa lie beyond its instruments; consciousness lies beyond its explanation.

Karma rests as saṃskāra in the subtle and causal bodies.

The grahas act where karma rests, and the gross body shows the result.

No physical force has been found because none is expected.

The grahas reach as far as karma reaches: waking, dream and deep sleep.

Turīya lies beyond them.

The chart ends where the kuṇḍalinī reaches the crown.

The order that shapes the body delivers the fruits of karma through it.

Its proof is readings that prove true. 

Sādara praṇāma. 🙏🏻
